summary: parseFile takes an optional `onWork` callback that it invokes immediately before each synchronous section (the tree-sitter parse and the content-token extraction), and it MUST be invoked here rather than at the call site. Verified this session by reproducing a real hang: parseFile awaits a grammar load and a file read, while the caller runs a batch of 100 through Promise.all, so every file in the batch gets past the call site before any of them reaches the CPU-bound work — a mark set out there named an innocent file while a different one span at 100% CPU. The rule the signature depends on is that no await may sit between an onWork call and the work it announces.

summary: parseFile does all of its awaits first (ensureParsersReady, the file read, and for Rust the findRustWorkspace lookup, now passed into parseByLanguage as rustWs), then calls onWork ONCE and runs the synchronous parseByLanguage + extractContentTokens as a single runWithTimeout call (see parse-guard.ts). parseByLanguage is synchronous and never returns null. On ParseTimeoutError it calls resetParsers() and returns pathOnlyParse(content) with timedOut: true; callers pass that to reportParseTimeout. onWork must still be called here, not at the call site: callers run batches of 100 via Promise.all, so a mark set before the awaits names the last file started, not the one spinning.

summary: parseFile does all of its awaits first (ensureParsersReady, the file read, for Rust the findRustWorkspace lookup passed into parseByLanguage as rustWs, and a second ensureParsersReady when parsersReady() is false because another file's timeout threw the runtime away while this one awaited), then calls onWork ONCE and runs the synchronous parseByLanguage + extractContentTokens as a single runWithTimeout call (see parse-guard.ts). On ParseTimeoutError it calls resetParsers() (which drops the whole web-tree-sitter runtime) and returns pathOnlyParse(content) with timedOut: true; callers pass that to reportParseTimeout. Tree-sitter errors are caught inside the extractors and logged as '[parser] Tree-sitter error', so a broken runtime does NOT throw out of parseFile: the file comes back silently with no exports/symbols (symptom of the detached-ArrayBuffer bug). onWork must still be called here, not at the call site: callers run batches of 100 via Promise.all, so a mark set before the awaits names the last file started, not the one spinning.
